native-send.description: Creates a message from the JSON body and answers with the record of the message just created, still queued. From there the mock drives the lifecycle on its own: queued, sent and delivered, or the failure the magic number stages. When the request carries a callbackUrl, every status change is posted there.

fields.name: to
fields.description: The recipient number in E.164 (+5511912340010) or in the national form (11912340010); the mock normalizes it to E.164.

fields.name: body
fields.description: The message text, from 1 to 1600 characters.

fields.name: from
fields.description: The sender in E.164 or an alphanumeric sender id of up to 11 characters; without it the mock uses the default sender.

fields.name: callbackUrl
fields.description: The http/https address that receives the status events of this message.

examples.name: curl
examples.value: curl -X POST 'http://localhost:8899/v1/messages' -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"to":"+5511912340010","body":"Seu código de verificação é 482913.","from":"AMA4DEVS"}'

responses.description: The message was created and entered the queue; the answer carries the whole record, with the queued status.
The to is not a valid phone number (invalid_to); the answer carries the code, the message and the field at fault.

error.message: Invalid 'To' phone number: use E.164, e.g. +5511912345678.

responses.description: The number ends in 0003, the magic suffix the API rejects (rejected_number).

error.message: The number +5511912340003 is rejected by the API (magic suffix 0003).

responses.description: The message text is required (empty_body): the mock refuses the send when the body comes empty.

native-list.description: Answers the messages that answer the query filters, in the order they were created, and how many there are. With wait, the answer waits up to 30 seconds for the first message that matches the filters, which makes the route useful for tests that wait for an event. The listing answers 200 even when there is no message at all.

params.name: to
params.description: Keeps the messages sent to this number.

params.name: from
params.description: Keeps the messages sent from this number or sender id.

params.name: number
params.description: Keeps the messages that have this number on either side, recipient or sender.

params.name: status
params.description: Keeps the messages with this status: queued, sent, delivered, undelivered, failed or received.

params.name: direction
params.description: Keeps the messages of one direction: outbound (app to handset) or inbound (handset to app).

params.name: q
params.description: Keeps the messages whose text, numbers or codes contain this value.

params.name: limit
params.description: The largest number of messages in the answer; when there are more, the newest ones stay.

params.name: after
params.description: The id of a message: the list carries only the messages created after it.

params.name: wait
params.description: Waits, in milliseconds, for the first message that answers the filters; 30000 at most.

responses.description: The list of the messages that answer the filters and how many there are; with no message, the list comes empty and count is zero.

native-get.description: Answers the requested message with its body, its current status and the history of its status changes. The id is SM followed by 32 hexadecimal digits, the same one the creation and the listing return. When the mock does not know the id, the answer is 404.

params.name: id
params.description: The id of the message: SM followed by 32 hexadecimal digits.

responses.description: The requested message, with the body, the current status and the history of the status changes.
The mock has no message with that id (not_found), which may have been deleted before.

native-delete.description: Removes the message from the mock and answers 204, with no body. The message leaves the listing and the panel stops showing it. When the id does not exist, the answer is 404 and nothing is deleted.

params.name: id
params.description: The id of the message: SM followed by 32 hexadecimal digits.

responses.description: The message was deleted; the answer comes with no body.
There is no message with that id (not_found), so nothing was deleted.

simple-send-get.description: It is the shortest way to send a message: the parameters travel in the query and the answer carries the status, the id, the normalized recipient and the number of segments. The message enters the queue as queued and follows the same lifecycle as the other APIs. When a field is wrong, the answer comes as status: error, with the code and the message of the error.

params.name: to
params.description: The recipient number in E.164 (+5511912340010) or in the national form (11912340010).

params.name: message
params.description: The message text, from 1 to 1600 characters; text and body are aliases of this field.

params.name: sender
params.description: The sender in E.164 or an alphanumeric sender id of up to 11 characters; from is its alias.

params.name: callbackUrl
params.description: The http/https address that receives the status events of this message.

responses.description: The message was accepted; the answer carries status, the id, the normalized recipient and the number of segments.
The recipient is not a valid number (invalid_to); the answer comes as status: error, with the code and the message of the error.

example.message: Invalid 'To' phone number: use E.164, e.g. +5511912345678.

simple-send-post.description: The same send as the GET version, with to, message, sender and callbackUrl in the JSON body (a urlencoded form works too). When a request carries both a body and a query, the body wins. The answer carries the status, the id, the normalized recipient and the number of segments, and the message follows the lifecycle of the queue.

fields.name: to
fields.description: The recipient number in E.164 (+5511912340010) or in the national form (11912340010).

fields.name: message
fields.description: The message text, from 1 to 1600 characters; text and body are aliases of this field.

fields.name: sender
fields.description: The sender in E.164 or an alphanumeric sender id of up to 11 characters; from is its alias.

fields.name: callbackUrl
fields.description: The http/https address that receives the status events of this message.

responses.description: The message was accepted; the answer carries status, the id, the normalized recipient and the number of segments.
The body carries no message text (empty_body); on POST the body wins over the query.

twilio-send.description: Creates a message from the To, From, Body and StatusCallback fields and answers the resource in the Twilio shape, with the dates in RFC 2822. Without a From, the default sender of the settings is used.

params.name: AccountSid
params.description: The account that signs the request; the mock ignores this value.

fields.name: To
fields.description: The number that receives the message, in the E.164 format.

fields.name: From
fields.description: The sender: an E.164 number or an alphanumeric sender id of up to 11 characters.

fields.name: MessagingServiceSid
fields.description: The messaging service in place of From; without a From, the default sender is used.

fields.name: Body
fields.description: The text of the message, up to 1600 characters.

fields.name: StatusCallback
fields.description: The URL that receives the status webhooks of this message.

responses.description: The message was created and the resource in the Twilio shape comes back in the answer.
The destination number is not E.164: the 21211 error comes back in the Twilio shape.

example.message: Invalid 'To' phone number: use E.164, e.g. +5511912345678.

responses.description: The body of the message is required: the 21602 error comes back in the Twilio shape.
The sender is neither E.164 nor alphanumeric: the 21212 error comes back in the Twilio shape.

example.message: Invalid 'From': use E.164 or an alphanumeric sender id (up to 11 characters).

twilio-list.description: Answers the newest messages first, narrowed by To and From, with the paging fields a Twilio client reads. PageSize is 50 by default and at most 1000.

params.name: AccountSid
params.description: The account that signs the request; the mock ignores this value.

params.name: To
params.description: Filters the messages sent to this number.

params.name: From
params.description: Filters the messages sent from this sender.

params.name: PageSize
params.description: How many messages the page holds: 50 by default, at most 1000.

responses.description: The page of messages comes back in the Twilio shape, with the count and the page links.

twilio-get.description: Answers one message in the Twilio shape. A sid the mock does not know comes back as the 20404 error.

params.name: AccountSid
params.description: The account that signs the request; the mock ignores this value.

params.name: MessageSid
params.description: The sid of the message to read.

responses.description: The message comes back in the Twilio shape.
The sid does not exist: the 20404 error comes back in the Twilio shape.

example.message: The requested resource /2010-04-01/Accounts/ACmock00000000000000000000000000/Messages/SMunknown00000000000000000000000000.json was not found

twilio-delete.description: Takes the message out of the mock. A sid the mock does not know comes back as the 20404 error.

params.name: AccountSid
params.description: The account that signs the request; the mock ignores this value.

params.name: MessageSid
params.description: The sid of the message to delete.

responses.description: The message was deleted; the answer has no body.
The sid does not exist: the 20404 error comes back in the Twilio shape.

example.message: The requested resource /2010-04-01/Accounts/ACmock00000000000000000000000000/Messages/SMunknown00000000000000000000000000.json was not found
